summary: Discovery call to understand Inkwell Labs' plan for a UX prototype using Redwood's API. Customer evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private due to PII in inputs and latency constraints for interactive UX. Discussed trial credits (time-to-first-token), security requirements (SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS), and next steps: provisioning credits, perf estimate, and a follow-up benchmark call.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
Latency vs cost for interactive UX
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-14 17:00 PST
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Marisol Chen (Redwood SE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood CSM), Avery Kim (CTO, Inkwell), Samir Rao (Lead Engineer), Nina Lopez (Product), Olivia Park (Security)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood. I'll let folks do quick intros then get into what you all are trying to do with the UX prototype.
[00:12] Avery: Hi, Avery here. CTO at Inkwell, we're building an AI-assisted composition tool for writers. Prototype goal is to power inline suggestions with low latency.
[00:20] Samir: Samir, I lead platform. We're most worried about PII in drafts and keeping latency under ~150ms tail for small completions.
[00:28] Nina: Nina, product. We're trying to ship a clickable prototype in 3 weeks for user research.
[00:34] Olivia: Olivia, security. I'll ask about data flow, retention, and encryption.
[00:39] Marisol: Marisol, SE. I focus on perf and routing—happy to dig into benchmarks and deployment options.
[00:45] Diego: Diego, CSM. I'll be the onboarding touchpoint.

[01:00] Jordan: Great. First, quick high level—Redwood offers the hosted API for fastest time-to-first-token with free credits. Dedicated is reserved capacity for consistent throughput and lower marginal cost, and Private is the VPC/on-prem option for regulated data. Given what you said about drafts having PII, Olivia, is that a blocker for hosted, or do you have controls that would make hosted acceptable?
[01:25] Olivia: Hosted is possible if we can guarantee no customer data is used outside of our account and there's strong encryption at rest and in transit, plus KMS integration. Also need audit logs and a SOC 2 report.
[01:37] Jordan: Yup, we have SOC 2 and ISO docs we can share, and customers can request dedicated tenancy or Private for extra isolation. We also support customer-managed keys via KMS for Private and Dedicated depending on setup.

[02:10] Samir: Quick question about time-to-first-token—how long to get devs from sign-up to a first working API call? We're on a tight timeline for the prototype.
[02:18] Marisol: For a PLG self-serve flow, typical is under an hour: sign up, we provision credits, you create an API key, and can hit the hosted endpoint. We also have SDK examples for Node and Python. For your interactive UX, we recommend streaming responses to display partial suggestions quickly which cuts perceived latency.
[02:42] Avery: That sounds promising. For the prototype, we want to test 1–2 models and evaluate a quantized model variant for cost. Can you comment on model parity across hosted vs dedicated?
[02:55] Marisol: Hosted has our curated catalog with verified perf profiles. Dedicated lets you pin model versions and use quantized variants for cost savings, but there's a short onboarding window for model onboarding. Private gives you the most control over model bits and kernel selection if you need on-prem quantization—tradeoff is setup time.

[03:25] Nina: How do we balance latency vs cost—our prototype will do lots of short completions (30–100 tokens). Any rules of thumb?
[03:31] Marisol: For short tokens, batching can be counterproductive if you need low tail latency. We typically recommend small batch sizes or continuous batching with latency SLOs disabled. KV/prefix caching helps a lot for repeated prefixes. For cost, quantized models (8-bit/4-bit) cut token compute but may slightly affect output distribution. We can run an estimate for your prompt shapes.

[04:05] Samir: Can you run an estimate for 512-token max completions with about 50 qps? It's just a back-of-envelope for budgeting.
[04:12] Marisol: Yes—I'll run perf & cost sim and share numbers. I'll assume a mix of streaming completions and small non-streaming for longer flows.

[04:30] Jordan: On the security front, Olivia, Redwood supports SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, encryption in transit, and options for customer KMS for Dedicated/Private. Any other must-haves?
[04:43] Olivia: We need to confirm data retention options—can you auto-delete logs, and what about transcript retention? Also, do you support bringing your own HSM for keys?
[04:54] Jordan: By default hosted keeps logs per policy but we can disable retention or set short retention for enterprise accounts. BYOK with KMS is available for Private; HSM integrations require a bit more work—I'll include our compliance notes.

[05:20] Nina: For the prototype, we won't need Private yet, but the plan is to evaluate hosted for speed to prototype, then if security blocks arise move to Dedicated for isolation. Does that sound like a normal path?
[05:29] Jordan: Very common. Many customers start PLG-hosted to validate UX, then shift to Dedicated when they need consistent capacity or better cost curve, and finally Private if compliance demands it.

[06:00] Samir: Can Redwood do a soft traffic shaping? For example route internal prod traffic to Dedicated but keep dev and research on hosted?
[06:09] Marisol: Yes we have smart routing policies—routes can be by API key, region, or customer tag. You can set fallback rules if Dedicated is saturated.

[06:35] Jordan: Any questions on billing and credits? We have a trial that gives teams credits to run experiments; credits are applied to hosted usage. Dedicated is contract-based, but you can do a pilot with reserved hours.
[06:47] Avery: How do credits map to token usage? We want to know if 50 credits will meaningfully cover the prototype.
[06:53] Jordan: Credits are effectively USD-equivalent; we'll map to token pricing per model. I'll provision 50 credits and Marisol will simulate the expected burn for your workflows so you can see runway.

[07:15] Olivia: On data residency—some of our users are EU-based; do you have region options and logs in particular regions?
[07:22] Marisol: Yes, hosted supports region selectors; Dedicated and Private can be instantiated in specific cloud regions. For EU residency we recommend spinning a Dedicated cluster in the region or Private for strict control.

[08:00] Samir: Let's talk about performance testing—if we want an apples-to-apples latency benchmark for our UI, what does Redwood need from us?
[08:07] Marisol: Ideally: a set of representative prompts (you said you'll share), desired sequence lengths, concurrency targets, and whether you use streaming. We'll run a small benchmark from our infra or provide scripts for you to run locally against hosted.
[08:25] Samir: We'll prepare a prompt set and a small harness. Good.

[09:00] Nina: One practical question—does Redwood expose request-level trace IDs we can attach to our logs to correlate UX latency?
[09:06] Marisol: Yes, every request has request_id in response headers and we expose traces in Console with per-request token breakdowns.

[09:30] Jordan: Any blockers on your side for starting the PLG trial?
[09:34] Avery: None technical. Security will review but for prototype we may be OK with hosted if retention is short and keys are managed.
[09:44] Olivia: I'll need the security pack and a short data flow diagram. Also curious about whether logs ever leave the region.
[09:52] Jordan: We'll include data flow and our regional guarantees in the pack.

[10:10] Samir: About model variants—if we want a lower-cost 4-bit quantized model, how much variance should we expect in output? We can't have hallucinations increasing in user docs.
[10:20] Marisol: There can be small distribution shifts. We recommend running an eval set of prompt/expected outputs—Redwood Optimize can suggest quant profiles and we can run regression checks. For prototype, stick with a verified hosted model then test a quantized variant in Dedicated.

[11:00] Jordan: Quick note on rollouts. We support canary and A/B deployment across model versions within Dedicated and Hosted; Private requires config but supports same principles.

[11:20] Nina: For our three-week cadence, what sequence do you recommend?
[11:25] Marisol: Week 1: provision credits, integrate SDK, smoke tests. Week 2: run bench and iterate prompts. Week 3: user research and decide whether to move to Dedicated pilot. We can run parallel perf tests if you want.

[11:50] Avery: That timeline is doable. Let's confirm responsibilities.

[12:00] Jordan: We'll: 1) provision trial credits and invite your devs, 2) send security docs, 3) SE to run perf estimates and bench once you send prompts. You: 1) share prompt sets & expected qps, 2) security will review docs and send questions.

[12:30] Olivia: One more, do you provide dedicated logging hooks for SIEM or a syslog forwarder?
[12:36] Diego: Yes we have integrations for log exports to S3 or to SIEM via secure transfer; we'll include options in the security pack.

[13:00] Samir: If we hit a scaling issue in the middle of a test, do you have burst capacity or autoscaling?
[13:07] Marisol: Dedicated supports autoscaling policies and burst options to ensure throughput. Hosted scales automatically but without reserved capacity—you might see transient throttles under extreme load but fallbacks exist.

[13:40] Nina: Are there any gotchas with streaming vs non-streaming in terms of cost?
[13:44] Marisol: Streaming sends tokens progressively; cost is still per token but perceived latency is lower. There is slight overhead for streams, but usually worth it for UX. We'll model that in the perf sim.

[14:10] Jordan: Any concerns about vendor lock-in?
[14:13] Avery: We don't want to build too deep custom logic tied to a single runtime.
[14:18] Marisol: Redwood exposes standard REST and SDKs and keeps model infra stable. We also provide exportable usage reports and recommend interface layers in your app to isolate calls—many customers do that as a best practice.

[14:45] Olivia: Data deletion policy—if a user requests deletion, what's the flow for hosted?
[14:50] Jordan: We can run deletion on request and provide you with deletion receipts; for stricter SLAs Dedicated/Private gives you more control.

[15:10] Samir: Ok let's walk through a hypothetical integration: we want inline completions triggered on keystroke with streaming partial tokens and finalization on enter. QPS expected 40–60. Does that map to hosted?
[15:25] Marisol: Yes, hosted is ideal to start. We'll recommend streaming + edge routing in a nearby region. For 40–60 qps short tokens, the main lever is avoiding large batch sizes.

[16:00] Jordan: Any contractual questions? We mentioned Dedicated is contract-based; pilot options are typically monthly reserved capacity.
[16:08] Avery: Nothing at this stage. We'll see after prototype results.

[16:30] Nina: When can we get the credits?
[16:33] Jordan: I'll provision the 50 credits today and invite your team; Diego will send calendar invites for the follow-up.

[16:45] Olivia: Please include who to contact for escalations and data incident response.
[16:49] Diego: We'll include the security contact matrix in the pack.

[17:10] Marisol: I'll follow up with the perf sim. Please put the prompt set in the shared folder or paste into the email.

[17:30] Jordan: Recap of next steps: Jordan send security + pricing, Marisol share perf sim, Jordan provision credits, Samir share prompts, Olivia send compliance Qs, schedule bench call for week of Dec 21. Anything else?
[17:44] Avery: That's it. Thanks everyone.
[17:47] Jordan: Great, appreciate your time. Talk soon.
[17:52] Call ends.
